paper.core_task: training LLMs for effective multiturn human-LLM collaboration

contributions.name: A training framework for multiturn LLM collaboration
contributions.author_claim_text: We introduce COLLABLLM, a novel and general training framework that enhances multiturn human-LLM collaboration.
contributions.description: A general training framework that uses a collaborative simulation to estimate long-term response impact, enabling LLMs to actively uncover user intent and provide insightful suggestions beyond simple request fulfillment.

contributions.name: A multiturn reward estimation method
contributions.author_claim_text: Its key innovation is a collaborative simulation that estimates the long-term contribution of responses using Multiturn-aware Rewards.
contributions.description: A method that estimates the long-term impact of a model response on future conversation turns via forward sampling and a reward combining task success, efficiency, and engagement.

contributions.name: A multiturn interaction benchmark
contributions.author_claim_text: We also devise a multiturn interaction benchmark with three challenging tasks such as document creation.
contributions.description: A new benchmark consisting of three multiturn tasks—document editing, code generation, and math problem solving—for training and evaluating collaborative LLMs.

novelty_claims.text: The authors propose a novel training framework, COLLABLLM, that incorporates a multi-turn reward estimation mechanism through collaborative simulation.
The paper introduces a novel approach to training LLMs for multi-turn collaboration by estimating multi-turn rewards through collaborative simulation.
The paper proposes a novel approach to training LLMs for multi-turn collaboration using a simulated user environment.
This paper introduces COLLABLLM, a novel training framework designed to enhance Large Language Models (LLMs) for effective multiturn human-LLM collaboration.
The paper introduces a novel approach to training LLMs for multiturn collaboration, addressing a critical gap in existing frameworks that primarily focus on single-turn interactions.
